question: Who founded the Prarthana Samaj in Mumbai in 1867?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Atmaram Pandurang**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Atmaram Pandurang was a social reformer and the founder of the **Prarthana Samaj in Mumbai in 1867.**
 
• The Prarthana Samaj was a movement for religious and social reform in Maharashtra based on earlier reform movements.
 
• The organization aimed to make people believe in one God and discard the caste system and superstitions.
 
• Atmaram Pandurang's efforts were directed towards promoting women's education and widow remarriage and opposing child marriage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prarthana Samaj**

 
 
• Prarthana Samaj was inspired by the Brahmo Samaj founded by** Raja Ram Mohan Roy in Bengal.**
 
• It was established by Atmaram Pandurang in 1867 to reform the social practices and religious beliefs of the Hindus in Maharashtra.
 
• The Samaj's principles were based on the teachings of Christianity and the ancient Hindu scriptures, advocating monotheism and discarding idol worship.
 
• Prominent members of the Prarthana Samaj included Justice** Mahadev Govind Ranade, R.G. Bhandarkar, and N.G. Chandavarkar**, who played significant roles in the social reform movements in Maharashtra.
 
 
 
• **Brahmo Samaj**
 
 
• Founded by **Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1828 in Kolkata,** Brahmo Samaj was one of the earliest reform movements in India.
 
• The Samaj aimed at purifying Hinduism and promoting monotheism, rejecting the caste system, idol worship, and rituals.
 
• It played a crucial role in the abolition of the practice of Sati and child marriage, and the promotion of widow remarriage and women's education.
 
• Raja Ram Mohan Roy is often called the **"Father of Modern India**" due to his efforts to modernize Indian society.
 
 
 
• **Social Reform Movements in India**
 
 
• During the** 19th and early 20th centuries,** India witnessed several social reform movements aimed at addressing social issues like caste discrimination, gender inequality, and religious superstitions.
 
• Prominent social reformers included** Raja Ram Mohan Roy, Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, Jyotirao Phule, and Swami Vivekananda.**
 
• These movements played a significant role in shaping modern Indian society by advocating for education, women's rights, and social equality.
 
• The reforms laid the groundwork for India's struggle for independence and the subsequent formation of a democratic and secular nation.
